note: CAF Online notes Egypt were the only team at AFCON 2025 to make 11 changes to the starting XI in a group-stage match, and reads it as squad depth and Hassan's repeated message that every player is ready and trusted.

CAF Online says Hassan kept faith in goalkeeper El-Shenawy despite criticism linked to his club form and a goal conceded in every match he played; the keeper answered with key saves and Man of the Match against South Africa.
CAF Online acknowledges Hassan has faced criticism over Egypt's style of play but argues results (a third AFCON semi-final since 2017 after the 3-2 quarter-final win) support his approach.

Daily News Egypt's report has Shobeir saving Taremi's 11th-minute penalty after Saber's 5th-minute goal, and describes Trezeguet and Salah as Egypt's attacking duo up front, whereas FotMob records the shape as 4-2-3-1 (formation labels differ by source).
AP reports that after going 2-0 up on Zico's 67th-minute goal Egypt fell into a defensive shell to protect the lead, and Argentina scored in the 79th and 83rd minutes and in stoppage time.
AP describes Egypt's second goal as coming from a break started by Salah out of his own half, and the winning goal as starting when Salah was dispossessed while dribbling into the box.

ESPN quotes forward Zico saying Egypt did not treat 2-0 as a finished game, which sits against AP's description of a defensive shell; Hassan's own post-match comments centred on refereeing (a disallowed goal and an unchecked foul) rather than tactics.

Mada Masr columnist view: at AFCON 2025 Hassan set Egypt up defensively and it took them to fourth place; at the 2026 World Cup he showed a clear change toward more attacking approaches and better game management.

Mada Masr writes that Hassan, like predecessors, relied on Salah as the main attacking outlet (the 'pass-to-Salah team' label) but built more structure around him, and quotes Hassan claiming he used Salah in a position nobody had seen him play.
Mada Masr flags Hassan's decision to take a fourth goalkeeper in the 26-man World Cup squad at the expense of an extra striker; Egypt were the only team to do so.
